A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReservoirTTA and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–K. The original material can be matched across renumbering and relocation, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification and segmentation experiments, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and temporally correlated-stream results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds object-level style-shift evaluations, gradual-severity tests, and further ablations.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure in Equations (7)–(14) and Algorithm 1 is retained: VGG style extraction, online clustering, specialist initialization and adaptation, and parameter ensembling. Alternative extractors, distances, and initializations are tested as ablations rather than adopted as method changes.

E1.justification: v3 adds DomainNet-126 and PACS, extending evaluation to object-level style shifts, and introduces a gradual-severity CIFAR-100-C stream. The original corruption, segmentation, and temporally correlated CIFAR-10-C coverage remains.

E2.justification: Table 11 adds RDumb w/ VGG, a domain-aware reset comparator, alongside RDumb and EATA+ReservoirTTA. Existing benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. The newly cited Contrastive TTA paper supplies experimental precedent, not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: New protocols train ResNet-50 separately on each DomainNet/PACS source domain and cycle through the remaining three domains 20 times. The gradual CIFAR-100-C test cycles severities 1–5–1 with Kmax of 16 or 64. New controls also test detector-triggered resets and alternative initialization and assignment procedures; retained experiments have no stated setting revisions.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends the existing analyses with source-backbone versus VGG extraction, Euclidean/cosine/KL assignments, top-three ensemble initialization, and resetting versus specialist reuse (Appendices D–F and I). It also adds quantile-dependent domain counts and gradual-severity robustness results. Temporal-correlation and batch-order analyses already existed in v2.

E5.justification: Existing five-run/seed averaging and Table 5's across-configuration mean and standard-deviation summaries are retained. Figure 4 redisplays an existing seed-dependent domain-detection analysis. No new uncertainty-estimation practice or revised run count is stated.

E6.justification: Matched original results remain unchanged, but substantial new results are reported. Tables 24–25 give EATA+ReservoirTTA versus EATA mean errors of 35.13 versus 35.92 on DomainNet-126 and 28.68 versus 29.38 on PACS. Table 26 reports gradual-shift errors of 25.06/24.95 versus EATA's 25.41. Additional ablation results are also new; these are not same-setting improvements between versions.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1, Proposition 3 replaces the uncentered gradient second-moment expression with expected gradient variance in its formal assumption. The resulting variance bound, remaining propositions, and proof arguments are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the empirical contribution to include object-level style shifts on DomainNet-126 and PACS. The central claims about domain-specialized adaptation, stability, and reduced forgetting remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New discussion attributes VGG's advantage to texture priors and architecture independence, and interprets the reset comparison as evidence for specialist reuse. The conclusion adds a limitation concerning updates on every batch regardless of convergence and suggests adaptive update triggering; this is a proposed improvement, not an implemented component.

D1.justification: Appendix H and Table 10 add DomainNet/PACS optimizers, learning rates, batch sizes, and dataset access links. Existing hardware and code-access information remains. A new inconsistency limits reproducibility: Table 10 prints DomainNet's learning rate as 2.5×10^4, whereas Appendix H states 2.5×10^-4.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for Contrastive TTA, PACS, DomainNet, and minimax-entropy domain adaptation, while removing Un-mixing Test-time Normalization Statistics. The related-work organization and positioning against existing TTA approaches are largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and Appendices A–K remain intact. v3 makes localized paragraph rewrites, adds descriptive subheadings and analysis paragraphs, shortens some captions, and replaces the preprint footer with NeurIPS 2025 conference information.

P2.justification: Substantial new tabular material presents extractor, distance, reset, object-style, and gradual-shift evaluations in Tables 7, 9, 11, and 24–26. Original figures are retained; new Figure 4 redisplays ReservoirTTA panels from the existing domain-detection analysis. The temporal-correlation table is reformatted into two visit blocks, with its results preserved.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, the object-style evaluations and targeted ablations provide useful additional support for generalization and key design choices. Reporting errors limit the gain: Appendix K misidentifies PACS's largest improvement as coming from cartoon rather than sketch, Section 5.2 mixes reset averages with visit-20 results, and Table 10 conflicts with Appendix H on the DomainNet learning rate. The added evidence still yields a limited net improvement.
